No. In your installed Vitest (5.0.3), `expect.poll` races every callback call against its own `timeout` (1000 ms by default; you can change it per call or with `expect.poll.timeout` in the config). If the callback never settles, the poll stops when that timeout runs out and fails with `expect.poll() function didn't resolve in time.` If an earlier attempt had already thrown, it reports that earlier error instead (`node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.C4tKZ0yW.js:7593-7596`). An assertion that never settles gets the same treatment.

When the timeout fires, the callback also receives a `{ signal }` that gets aborted, so you can pass it to `fetch` or similar calls to cancel the work that's hanging. The test-level `testTimeout` (5 s by default) is a second backstop, unless you've turned it off with `0`.
